quick_ref.Theme: The Hero Academy — Describe Your Hero Look

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The "Mirror Game" Concept
content: Problem: Students frequently confuse "is" (states) with "has" (possession), resulting in errors like "I am long hair" or "She has tall."
Solution: We use the "Mirror Game" to visually distinguish between what a person is (their state: tall, short, big, small) and what a person has (their physical features: hair, eyes, glasses).

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce physical features and the contrast between "is" and "has".
Session 2: Expand descriptions with adjectives (long, short, curly, straight).
Session 3: Consolidate full physical descriptions of self and others.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Ask the student: "Are you tall or short?" -> Student: "I am short." "Do you have big eyes?" -> Student: "I have big eyes."
S2 pull-out: Ask the student: "What kind of hair does she have?" -> Student: "She has long curly hair."
Communicative task (Section 8): Mirror Partners. Students describe their partner's appearance using "is" and "has".

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  The Mirror Partners
content: Look at the heroes at the Academy!
Max is tall. He has short hair. He has brown eyes. He has big glasses.
Luna is short. She has long hair. Her hair is curly. She has big brown eyes.
Tom has straight hair. His hair is black. He has small ears.
All heroes look different. But all heroes are special!
Today, the students play the Mirror Game.
Max looks at Luna. "You are short," says Max.
"You have long hair. Your hair is curly and brown."
Luna looks at Max. "You are tall," says Luna.
"You have short hair. Your hair is straight and black."
"Yes, I have small eyes," says Max.
They laugh together. They are great mirror partners!

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W3: tall, short, hair, eyes, long
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (tall, short, hair, eyes, long) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: "is" vs "has" (State vs Possession)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: "is" vs "has" (State vs Possession).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Identity & Environment — The Mirror Game"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Identity & Environment — The Mirror Game".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (tall, short, hair, eyes, long usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.
